paragraphs: Posted by Mia. Last month, May and I found a small nest in a tree near the school library. Many people pass the tree every day, but nobody saw the nest. It was high on a branch, and green leaves almost hid it. I made an album about the nest, and it includes five photos. I used my mom's camera, and May wrote the words under each photo. Teacher Kim read them first.

Photo one shows the nest on a Monday. It is small and round, and it has three small blue eggs. A little brown bird sits near the nest and looks at us. The brown feathers suit the branch, because the bird is hard to see. It was a quiet place, and we liked it very much. We stood far from the tree, because Teacher Kim told us not to touch the nest. Photo two shows the nest on Wednesday. The mother bird sits on the three eggs, and her head is down. The tree is old, and the wind is soft. She does not move for ten minutes.

Photo three shows the nest on Friday. There is one egg, and there are two small gray birds with big open mouths. Their eyes are closed, and they have almost no feathers. The mother bird stands on the branch with a small insect in her beak. The birds were so small! Even Leo was quiet, and Leo is never quiet. May whispered, "Look at the mouths!"

Photo four shows the nest ten days later, on a Monday. Now there are three small birds, and they are bigger than before. They have brown feathers, and their eyes are open. Both parent birds come and go every minute with food. The nest is full, and it looks very small. Photo five shows the nest on the Thursday after that. The nest is empty, and a small brown bird sits on a branch near it.

We did not see the small birds again. We were happy, but we missed them. Maybe they are now in another tree, and maybe they are near us. I like my album because it shows five days of one small family. Do you know a tree with a nest? Please do not touch a nest, and look from far away.
text.summary: Mia and May watch a small nest in a tree near the school library. Mia's album has five photos, and the words under them show that the eggs hatch and the young birds leave, but the text never says it.
